facts.current_docstring_summary: Given a K x K relation core matrix Z, uses scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on -abs(Z) to find the diagonal-maximizing permutation (Hungarian algorithm). structure_score = min(matched diagonal-under-permutation entries) / max(unmatched entries). Returns (perm: list[int], trusted: bool) where trusted = structure_score > structure_threshold. If total_mass of abs(Z) is <=1e-15, short-circuits to (list(range(K)), False) (identity perm, not trusted). If max_unmatched is ~0 (no off-diagonal mass), structure_score is set to float('inf') (always trusted in that case).
notable_facts: trusted=True (structure_score > threshold) means a confidently clean relabelling exists and IS applied by callers; trusted=False means genuine mixed coupling and the raw identity permutation is used as-is — this is the interpretation stated directly in the docstring, consistent with STRUCTURE_SCORE_THRESHOLD's own comment.

facts.current_docstring_summary: Computes a reconstruction-space per-community share vector for one relation. Gets (perm, trusted) from _hungarian_relabel_relation; uses the corrected permutation p if trusted, else identity. Computes c_u = U_final_f1.T @ U_final_f1, c_v = U_final_f2.T @ U_final_f2, and total = trace(Z.T @ c_u @ Z @ c_v) — the relation's entire reconstructed Frobenius mass (diagonal AND off-diagonal, i.e. including cross-community interference). within[k] = Z[k, p[k]]^2 for each community k (this reduces algebraically to the within-community reconstructed mass because U_norm's columns are unit-L2 by construction). Returns within/total elementwise, or a uniform 1/K vector if total <= 1e-15.
notable_facts: This is the function CLAUDE.md's own §4.18 design section names as production's own mass mechanism for the (superseded, rejected) Z_scaled-based domain-balance draft — it is used by evaluate_dimensional_collapse (via a loop over Z_final.items()), NOT by evaluate_domain_balance (which is U_prob-based and does not call this function at all).

Chosen over a simpler diagonal-sum share specifically because it is sensitive to cross-community interference (a relation whose mass is mostly off-diagonal contributes correspondingly little share to any community, rather than being forced to sum diagonal entries to 1).

facts.current_signature_or_value: def evaluate_socio_semantic_reality(U_prob, raw_data, active_matrices, max_monopoly, presence_masks=None):
facts.current_docstring_summary: Computes a combined socio-semantic reality penalty in two parts. Part A: for each community k, propagates article-level weight W_art = U_prob['art'][:,k] outward through the active M_* relations (parent/child/cousin/atom/fringe, following the actual topology), and for each of 4 target semantic facets (core_child_he, cousin_he, core_atom, fringe_atom) compares a weighted average of the model's own U_prob loading (weighted by the propagated empirical weight) against a live-entity-masked baseline mean loading; squared-ceiling penalty when weighted_avg falls short of baseline. Part B: using the same propagated per-community weights captured as empirical_mass_capture, computes a normalized Shannon entropy per entity (how 'universal'/doxa-like a semantic node's empirical usage is) and multiplies a squared max_monopoly-ceiling penalty (on the model's own max learned U_prob loading) by that entropy — i.e. only penalizes hoarding of high-entropy/universal terms, not niche ones. Final: socio_semantic_pen = (Penalty_A + Penalty_B) / 2.0.
notable_facts: DOCSTRING/BEHAVIOR MISMATCH: the function's docstring explicitly states 'Returns: socio_semantic_pen (float)... Penalty_A (float)... Penalty_B (float)' (three named return values), but every actual return statement in the body returns a SINGLE value: `return 1.0` (the K<2 early-exit guard, line ~1144) and `return float(socio_semantic_pen)` (the normal path, line 1333). Penalty_A and Penalty_B are computed internally but never returned. The single call site (evaluate_complete_solution, line 1506) correctly assigns the return to a single variable `socio_semantic_pen = evaluate_socio_semantic_reality(...)`, i.e. the call site's usage matches the actual 1-value behavior, not the docstring's stated 3-value behavior.
The K<2 early-return path returns the bare Python literal `1.0`, not `float(1.0)` explicitly, but this is already a native float so no JSON-serializability issue.

presence_masks is optional (defaults to None) — when None, Part A's baseline and Part B's valid_mask fall back to using ALL rows (dead entities included), not just live ones. In production it is always passed (evaluate_complete_solution always supplies presence_masks), so the None-fallback path is a defined-but-effectively-unused branch in the current call graph — worth noting for anyone editing based on 'presence_masks is optional' language.

target_facets is hardcoded to exactly 4 facets: ['core_child_he', 'cousin_he', 'core_atom', 'fringe_atom'] — parent_he is NOT included (this matches the open, undecided ticket 66 in CLAUDE.md about whether to add it).

facts.current_docstring_summary: For each active anchor relation (an anchor being any relation key present in both Z_final and the semantic_anchors frozenset), and for each community k, computes a symmetric cohesion ratio: diagonal_val / (0.5*(row_sum+col_sum)+eps), clipped to [0,1]. Averages this ratio across all active anchors for each community (the 'Mean Anchor Rule', allowing polycentric communities that are crisp at one semantic resolution but noisier at another). weakest_mean = the minimum such mean cohesion score across all K communities. coherence_pen = squared ceiling: (max(0, target_coherence - weakest_mean) / target_coherence)^2. Returns (coherence_pen: float, weakest_mean: float).
notable_facts: Returns (0.0, np.nan) immediately if no anchors from semantic_anchors are active in Z_final — this nan is only ever logged via trial.set_user_attr, and coherence_pen (0.0, not nan) is what actually feeds sociological_penalty, per the file's own resolved ticket 22 register entry.

facts.purpose_one_line: Post-hoc resampling null for the per-community domain-balance measure: asks how large |r_k-0.5| a model reports from sharpness (mean U_prob row-max) and headcount differences between social/semantic entities alone, with truth constructed to be exactly proportionally balanced (community-size vector p shared by both domains), i.e. no genuinely mono-domain community exists in the null by construction.
local_reimplementations: domain_rows() - pools live U_prob rows by domain from cached fit (thin wrapper, not duplicating diagnostic_blocks logic per se)

Self-check block explicitly asserts its own pooled-row reading against diagnostic_blocks.domain_balance_r_k (tolerance 1e-5, float32 vs float64 rounding) -- i.e. script deliberately duplicates the reading path and verifies agreement rather than blindly trusting either
notable_facts: Uses CACHED fits only (fit_or_load, no refit) -- reads the same fits domain_balance_measurement.py used.

Two nulls: N0 ('balanced truth, own sharpness and size' -- each entity keeps its own sorted membership profile but which community holds its top value is drawn from one common pooled community-size vector p) and N1 ('sharpness equalised' -- both domains draw entity profiles from the SAME pooled profile set). N0 minus N1 isolates the sharpness contribution specifically.

Statistics computed: per-fit mean and max of |r_k-0.5| over communities; observed value compared to its null distribution via one-sided p=(1+#null>=obs)/(B+1); 95th percentile of N0's max-dev used as the detection threshold for the positive-control power analysis.

Positive-control/power block: injects a known-size delta into one community's true community-size vector (function inject()) and records detection rate against the N0 95th-percentile threshold -- i.e. measures the SMALLEST true imbalance this measure can detect given this corpus's sharpness/size, on a POST-HOC RESAMPLING null, not a full-pipeline refit.

Explicitly states in its own header what it does NOT cover: entities are assigned independently in this null (real entities are clumped -- e.g. a many-author article pulls all its authors into one community -- which is a structural, not domain-specific, cause of imbalance the null does not capture), and it is a different quantity from FINDINGS §21's seed-to-seed reproducibility noise.

Script-level conclusion is NOT stated as a single verdict in the file; it prints per-cell observed vs null mean/max dev and p-values for the user to read. It is explicitly framed (in its header) as a precursor/narrower test than domain_balance_planted_null.py, which the header for the latter says supersedes it (this script 'resampled MEMBERSHIPS post-hoc and so could not capture what the optimizer itself contributes').

On success it keeps every already-completed (slice,config,K) cell exactly as recorded and the main loop skips those cells, running only the missing ones; every completed cell (not just at the very end) triggers checkpoint() with an atomic write (tmp file + os.replace) so a mid-run kill cannot leave a truncated file; each resume appends one entry (timestamp, cells_already_complete count, prior_elapsed_sec, PYTHONHASHSEED, SLURM_JOB_ID) to the output's 'resume_events' list; elapsed_sec_so_far stays cumulative across resumes.

notable_facts: CONFIRMED: this is the one script (of the 5, and per the task's note the one of ~40 in the wider cluster) that GATES/refuses on a BLOCKS_VERSION mismatch rather than merely recording it. Exact check, load_resume_state(): `if prior.get("blocks_version") != BLOCKS_VERSION: problems.append(f"blocks_version {prior.get('blocks_version')} != current {BLOCKS_VERSION}")` followed by `if problems: raise SystemExit("[resume] checkpoint incompatible with this run: " + "; ".join(problems))`. This gate only fires on a RESUME=1 run against an existing checkpoint -- a normal (non-resume) run never compares BLOCKS_VERSION against anything, it just writes the current value into new output.
